messages:
Maya: Quick sync — customer X wants a pilot that (1) surfaces per-route batching/caching/quantization recommendations and (2) fires eval-triggered alerts when quality drops. They want to start with 3 critical routes. What's realistic for an MVP?
Sam: For MVP we should probably limit to read-only recs + a webhook alert. Full auto-apply is risky. :+1:
Jin: Agree. Need to define the eval signals — e.g., BLEU/ROUGE or model-specific embedding drift + a small set of labeled prompts. How many evals do they have?
Rosa: Customer has ~500 labeled examples across the 3 routes but not evenly distributed. They're fine with a manual onboarding flow to tag important prompts.
Tom: Launch criteria we should consider: precision of recs (>=75% judged useful in pilot), alert false-positive rate < 10%, onboarding <= 2 hours for customer engineer. Also SLA for webhook delivery.
Maya: Good checklist. Propose scope: (A) recommendations API that returns ranked recs for batching/caching/quant profiles + a short rationale, (B) eval-triggered alerts that compare rolling evals to baseline and call webhook + in-console notification, (C) an onboarding guide for mapping routes and seed prompts. Keep auto-apply out of scope.
Sam: Implementation notes from infra perspective: start with an offline job that ingests request traces and simulates batching/caching impact (we already have trace sampler). Output is JSON like `{\n  \"route\": \"/api/chat\",\n  \"recs\": [ { \"type\": \"batch\", \"batch_size\": 8, \"expected_q_loss\": 0.01, \"savings_p95\": 0.32 }, ... ]\n}`
Sam: Minimal API:
```
POST /v1/optimize/recs
body: { routes: ["/api/chat"], lookback_hours: 72 }
returns: { recommendations: [...] }
```
Keep auth the same as Redwood API.
Jin: For eval-triggered alerts: we should support two signal types — metric regression (delta on eval metric) and embedding drift (KS test on embedding distribution). Example config:
```
{\n  \"route\": \"/api/chat\",\n  \"alert_rules\": [ { \"type\": \"metric_regression\", \"metric\": \"qa_accuracy\", \"threshold_pct\": 5, \"window_mins\": 60 }, { \"type\": \"embedding_drift\", \"p_value_threshold\": 0.01 } ]\n}
```
On breach -> POST to customer webhook + create alert in Console.
Rosa: Customer success: they want a QA workflow for verifying recs before applying. Suggest we add an action to export recs as CSV + a simple UI where they can accept/reject per-route. Otherwise their legal ops won't sign.
Maya: Ok include a lightweight accept/reject UI in Console (read-only for MVP, no auto-apply). That becomes part of acceptance criteria.
Tom: Risk/mitigation notes: (1) If recs degrade quality, need rollback path — since MVP is read-only that's OK. (2) Rate limits on trace ingestion — set 1M events/day cap per pilot. (3) Alert spam — require two-window confirmation before firing to webhook.
Sam: Timeline idea: 3 sprints to deliver core recs engine + API + webhook alerts basic integration. Sprint 4 for Console accept/reject and docs. Can do a pilot onboarding/runbook by end of sprint 5.
Jin: Data requirements: need traces + per-request latencies, token counts, model variant info, and a seed eval set. Also need a way to get embeddings for drift tests (can reuse embeddings pipeline).
Rosa: I'll coordinate with customer for the seed eval set and onboard engineers for UAT. Also will surface acceptance checklist items: rec usefulness survey, alert precision, onboarding time.
Maya: Decision points for PM/eng: 1) include quantization profile suggestions (e.g., 4-bit vs 8-bit) — pros: cost wins; cons: potential quality regressions. I'd lean include but mark as 'experimental' and surface expected quality delta. 2) scope of batching recs complexity: start with simple suggestions (batch_size per route) not request-shaping.
Sam: +1 to experimental quant profiles. We'll include expected_q_loss estimate and a confidence bucket.
redwood-bot: Reminder: Weekly pilot sync scheduled tomorrow 10:00 AM. Calendar invite sent.
Maya: Next steps for this thread: Sam/Jin to draft API + config schema by EOD Thursday, Rosa to confirm eval set by Friday, Tom to draft acceptance criteria doc. We'll review in pilot sync. :rocket:
